geometry: Simple unsealed faucet drain pocket with a round underside drip hole
user_quote: It just needs to have a hole, and not such a large one, so that if we get water up there we get the drip.
purpose: Visible warning discharge into the bowl during a major fault; incidental escape into the housing is accepted by Derek.
preservation_method: Current cavity-wall and interstice changes are bounded between tip stations 30 and 68; both old and new port cutters are within stations 20 to 78. Base ends before station zero. Joint, display/retention and dispense-face construction is unchanged.
scope: Nominal geometry and clearance only. Hole area is a dimension comparison, not a flow rating. Prior sealed-cavity hydraulic and seat witnesses do not apply to this unsealed warning outlet.
drip_hole_clearance_method: The whole straight hole cutter lies inward of the maximum radius at its cavity-side circular cap. The constant-radius soda centerline is at R; subtract its OD radius from that complete cap bound. Flavor/drain centerlines lie farther outward over this station range.
